diagram_math_checks.result: Each panel has exactly four endogenous vertices A,M,Y,L; A,M,Y are observed, L latent. G has L->A, L->Y, A->M, M->Y (four edges), with topological order L,A,M,Y. This is a finite full DAG in def-recursive-structural-causal-model-and-dag. L is explicitly distinguished from each exogenous U_v. Arrows encode causal graph edges, not morphisms between state spaces.

In G, A has only the outgoing edge A->M and M has only M->Y. Thus its unique directed A-to-Y path is A->M->Y, containing M. The other A-to-Y skeleton path A<-L->Y is not directed from A. This illustrates Statement (i) and the no-bypass premise used in Proof 1.3 and 3.1.

By the graph-operation clause of def-d-separation-in-a-dag, G_underline A removes A->M and retains L->A, L->Y, M->Y (three edges). Its skeleton is the chain A-L-Y-M. The unique A-to-M path A<-L->Y<-M has collider Y, with no conditioned descendant under empty conditioning, so it is inactive. This illustrates Statement (ii), consistent with its use in Proof 1.2.

G_underline M removes M->Y and retains L->A, L->Y, A->M (three edges). Its skeleton is the chain M-A-L-Y. Its unique M-to-Y path M<-A<-L->Y has internal noncolliders A and L. Conditioning on A blocks it under the active-path definition, establishing the displayed example of Statement (iii), the premise used in Proof 1.3-1.4.

The captions expressly describe a single example, not all DAGs satisfying the theorem, and no probability or commutativity assertion is inferred from drawing alone. The full original rigorous proof remains byte-unchanged before the appended Remarks and independent of this figure.
